newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Govt to spend NZ$19.9 mln on border control.
newsitem.headline: NZ Govt to spend NZ$19.9 mln on border control.

text.p: The government will spend NZ$19.9 million over the next three years on a new border control strategy to protect New Zealand's environment and primary industries from hazards such as fruitfly, Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith said on Tuesday.

"New Zealand received a clear warning with this year's fruitfly scare, which had the potential to put at risk our $1.4 billion horticulture industry and which will have cost taxpayers $6.627 million by the middle of next year," Smith said in a statement.
Smith said the new strategy would substantially reduce the risk of future importations of fruitfly and other hazards.

"It will protect our horticulture industry from pests like fruitfly, our livestock industries from disease such as foot and mouth, our forestry estate from a vast array of exotic pests, and New Zealand's unique biological environment as a whole," Smith said.
He said the strategy would ensure that as the tourism industry expanded it would not jeopardise other vitally important industries.
He said that 2.6 million passengers entered New Zealand last year and significant further growth was anticipated.
Passengers from Asian countries were expected to increase 15 percent per annum and by 7.0 percent per annum from the rest of the world.

"This presents a massive challenge to our border control services. In the last financial year alone, almost 11.5 tonnes of fruit and vegetable material was seized at the border, of which 4.8 tonnes was undeclared," Smith said.
The new border control strategy had three components:

* approximately $16.5 million over three years for the imminent installation and ongoing staffing of seven high-tech X-ray machines at Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch International Airports and the International Mail centre in Auckland;
* a $2.0 million boost over three years to the quarantine detector dog programme;
* approximately $500,000 for an upgraded multi-lingual, multi-media awareness programme.

Smith said the aim of the strategy was to enable people from all countries to be informed about the risks to New Zealand, the risks of being caught with illegal material and the size of the penalties.

"Our message to travellers is clear: welcome to New Zealand, but if you are bringing illegal material into New Zealand you will be caught by our state of the art technology and you will face fines of up to $100,000 and five years in jail," he said.
Smith said the new strategy would give New Zealand an 80 percent-plus detection rate, putting it up with the best in the world. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
